youtube.title: Poon Lim: How Did He Survive 133 Days Alone at Sea?
youtube.description:
Poon Lim survived 133 days alone on a raft in the Atlantic. How does one man stay alive that long with a few tins of food and nothing else?

In November 1942, a German U-boat torpedoed the SS Benlomond, and Poon Lim, a Chinese steward, was the only survivor. When his supplies ran out, he turned a nail from the raft into a fishhook and caught fish, seabirds and even a shark, until Brazilian fishermen found him on April 5, 1943.

Subscribe to Stickstory for a true survival story every day. Could you last one week on that raft? Tell me in the comments!

scenes.text: He survived 133 days alone on a raft.
scenes.visual: Open Atlantic, nothing to the horizon: a small square wooden raft (planks, a water keg, two tins) rocks on the swell, Poon Lim sitting on it, worried, looking around; gulls drift across; a big dark swell rolls through the foreground. In the hook frame the cover's big shocked fez narrator stands at the lower left.

scenes.text: In 1942, a U-boat sank his ship.
scenes.visual: Side view of the sea: a big cargo steamer (black hull, red boot-top, white bridge, funnel smoking) at the right, a surfaced U-boat at the far left; on 'U-boat' a bubble track races from the U-boat to the hull; on 'sank' a gold-and-red explosion and a white water column, the camera shakes, then the steamer lists and slides under the water line while black smoke rises; red handwritten 'NOV 23, 1942' at the top right.

scenes.text: Poon Lim, a Chinese steward, was the only survivor.
scenes.visual: Close shot at sea level: Poon Lim's head and stroking arm in the water as he swims towards the empty raft, splashes behind him, then grabs the raft's edge; a dark swell rolls in the foreground; on 'only' a red box 'ONLY SURVIVOR' pops in above him.

scenes.text: So when his food ran out,
scenes.visual: Close-up from above on the raft's deck planks filling the frame (sea beyond the far edge, the water keg at the left): an opened tin tips over empty on 'ran out' with a red handwritten 'EMPTY'; a single nail head sits in the middle plank.

scenes.text: he bent a nail from the raft into a hook.
scenes.visual: Closer on the planks: a hand pulls a long rusty nail straight out of the middle plank (handwritten 'NAIL' on 'nail'); on 'raft' a second hand grips the shaft and the nail curls into a barbed fishhook; on 'hook' it glints gold and a red box 'HOOK!' pops in.

scenes.text: It worked: fish, seabirds, even a shark!
scenes.visual: Split view at the surface: the raft with Poon Lim (bigger) dropping his line at the left, seaweed hanging below; underwater the line runs to the hook; on 'fish' a fish bites and is jerked up; on 'seabirds' a gull glides down and lands on the raft; on 'shark' a big shark glides in fully under the raft, Poon Lim jumps in shock and a red box 'SHARK!' pops in; a school of small fish fills the deep.

Wide ocean: a small cargo steamer on the far horizon at the right steams away out of frame; on the raft mid-frame Poon Lim waves and shouts, the fez narrator stands beside him waving both arms at the ship; on 'stopped' the ship is gone past, Lim sits down and the narrator jumps in shock; a red box 'NOT ONE STOPPED' pops in; a shark fin cuts through the dark swell in the foreground.

scenes.text: A U-boat even saw him, and left.
scenes.visual: Medium shot: right next to the raft a German U-boat rises out of the water with foam, a lookout on the conning tower turns to Poon Lim, who waves both arms; on 'left' the U-boat sails off to the right and dives, Lim drops his arms, worried; red box 'IT LEFT HIM'; dark swell in the foreground.

scenes.text: Day 133: Brazilian fishermen found him. A world record.
scenes.visual: Near the coast of Brazil (green land on the horizon): a card at the top counts 'DAY 1' up to a red 'DAY 133'; a small fishing sailboat with three fishermen glides in from the right to the raft; on 'found' the fishermen wave and point and Poon Lim waves back, happy; a dark swell rolls in the foreground.

scenes.text: "I hope no one will ever have to break that record," he said.
scenes.visual: Close-up: Poon Lim's hand holds the bent-nail fishhook up against the sea and sky, his face beside it, the hook glints gold; giant Fraunces words '“BREAK THAT' are on screen from the start, then 'RECORD.”' springs in a red box on 'record'.

scenes.text: Subscribe for a true story like this every day.
scenes.visual: Callback card: 'ONE RAFT.' then 'ONE NAIL.' with 'NAIL.' in a red box; the fez narrator now stands on the big raft in the foreground, holding the fishhook up and waving at the viewer.
